learning: If progress holds at about 0.138 (oval) and 0.148 (s-bend) with line loss near 1.0, the offset 0.06 m is neutral to slightly positive, and the next lever is per-track telemetry on where the single loss occurs. If progress falls, the optimum forward offset is at or near 0.05 m, and the remaining lever is the controller rather than the geometry.
notes: Complete runnable package: the iteration 7 baseline with sensor y moved from 0.05 m to 0.06 m. Controller and all other geometry are unchanged, so the race isolates the forward offset. All values are inside the contract limits.
rationale: The Builder's proposal changes one geometry lever against the iteration 7 baseline: sensor y moves from 0.05 m to 0.06 m, with 12 mm sensors and the same x spacing (-0.02 to +0.02 m). Iteration 7 confirmed the baseline at 52.28 (oval progress 0.138, s-bend 0.148, line loss 1.0 to 1.1 per run on oval and s-bend, 2.0 on slalom). Iteration 8 showed that an 8 mm footprint lowers progress on all tracks (oval 0.133, s-bend 0.143, slalom 0.097) and raises slalom loss to 2.0, so 12 mm stays. Iteration 0 (y 0.05) beat iteration 2 (y 0.03), but y 0.06 has not been tested. The controller is held identical to the iteration 0 and 7 pairing (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.6, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], last_direction). That pairing matches the 5-sensor layout, and keeping it fixed means any change in progress or line loss comes from the sensor row alone. Wheel radius 0.03 m, wheel track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg and body are unchanged, since iteration 6 showed the wheel change cost s-bend progress. Expected, not measured: line loss about 1.0 per run on oval and s-bend, at or below 2.0 on slalom, and progress near the baseline. Any gain or loss in progress from the forward offset will show in the race.
